segments.title: 第99章 還疼嗎
segments.content:
Reigniting the Prime of Youth Chapter 99: Does It Still Hurt?

On the basketball court.

Li Luo stood inside the free-throw line.

Zhao Rongjun stood outside the three-point line.

Li Luo could only play defense, and Zhao Rongjun could only shoot three-pointers.

The two girls, however, could attack and defend without any rules.

"Zhusheng, step back a bit to shoot. I'll help you block him." Xu Youyu smiled and reached out, holding Li Luo back as she turned her head and shouted to Yan Zhusheng.

Yan Zhusheng was over 1.7 meters tall and had good athletic coordination. After getting the ball, she held it at her chest to build momentum and shot it toward the hoop.

But Li Luo in front of her had already executed a gorgeous spin, and with a light jump, he slapped the ball out of mid-air. It was caught by Zhao Rongjun outside the three-point line.

"Ah!" Xu Youyu hurriedly grabbed Li Luo's arm. "You! How are you harder to catch than a fish in water?"

Yan Zhusheng narrowed her eyes, a little unhappy about having her shot blocked. She quickly ran in front of Zhao Rongjun and raised her hands to defend.

It was unclear if he was intentionally throwing the game or if his hands went soft at the sight of a pretty girl in front of him, but Zhao Rongjun took a three-point shot.

The result was an airball.

After Xu Youyu got the ball, to prevent another block, she passed it to Yan Zhusheng and then grabbed Li Luo's arm to keep him from running around.

This time, with no obstructions at all, Yan Zhusheng smoothly scored a basket.

When Ying Chanxi and Qiao Xinyan arrived at the basketball court carrying a large bag of drinks, this was the scene they witnessed.

"This looks so fun," Qiao Xinyan said, watching them play so cheerfully. She couldn't help but feel a sense of anticipation. "Xixi, I've never played basketball before. Have you?"

Ying Chanxi shook her head. "Back in middle school, I asked Li Luo if we could play for fun, but he said girls were too bad at it and wouldn't let me."

"Huh?" Qiao Xinyan was taken aback. "Your cousin used to be so obnoxious... What kind of thing is that to say?"

"He's slowly getting a little better now." Ying Chanxi watched the four of them having fun on the court, squinting as she said, "It feels like he's become much more considerate."

As she spoke, Ying Chanxi had already walked to the edge of the court. She placed the plastic bag in her hand on a long bench and said to the people on the court, "I put the drinks here. Help yourselves to whatever you want."

"Alright, let's take a break then." Li Luo clapped his hands, signaling a halftime. "The score is 0 to 6. This guy Zhao Rongjun is unreliable. When did shooting a three-pointer become so hard for you?"

"Then why don't you shoot the threes and let Zhao Rongjun defend inside?" Xu Youyu asked with a grin.

"Let him defend?" Li Luo shook his head with a laugh. "What's the difference between that and having no one on defense?"

If Zhao Rongjun were to defend inside the free-throw line, he probably wouldn't even dare to look Xu Youyu and Yan Zhusheng in the eye.

"Just don't let me be on the same team as you," Zhao Rongjun said sullenly. "I'll focus on defending you."

"That's fine." Li Luo took a bottle of Minute Maid Pulpy from the plastic bag on the bench and chugged a few mouthfuls. "Let's split the six of us into two teams. Each guy with two girls, and the guys can't shoot. How about that?"

"That's a good idea." Xu Youyu expressed her support.

"Then I'll be on a team with Zhao Rongjun." Ying Chanxi walked over to Zhao Rongjun's side and looked at Li Luo. "You pick one too, then let Zhao Rongjun pick the next one."

"Then Yan Zhusheng," Li Luo said, pointing at his deskmate.

After all, Yan Zhusheng was more athletic and at least had enough strength to shoot. Not like some girls who struggled to even make a shot from under the basket.

Next was Zhao Rongjun's turn. He hemmed and hawed, looking left and right, before finally choosing Qiao Xinyan.

"Isn't this a guaranteed win?" Li Luo raised an eyebrow, gesturing at the height difference between the girls on both teams.

Needless to say, Yan Zhusheng was over 1.7 meters tall, which was quite rare among girls.

Xu Youyu herself wasn't short either, standing at around 168 cm.

Ying Chanxi and Qiao Xinyan were both about 1.6 meters, looking petite and cute.

"Let me reiterate, the guys can't shoot." Li Luo bounced the ball in his hand and slowly walked to the three-point line, preparing to inbound the ball.

"Why do you guys get to inbound first?" Ying Chanxi asked.

Li Luo paused for a moment, thinking they were just playing for fun.

But seeing Ying Chanxi's very serious expression, Li Luo chuckled and walked to the free-throw line. "How about this? If I make this free throw, we inbound. If I miss, you guys do."

"Fine, go ahead and shoot."

Li Luo took a free throw.

His form was very cool and standard, but he missed.

Ying Chanxi huffed, took the ball, and handed it to Zhao Rongjun. "We'll inbound."

Zhao Rongjun obediently took the ball, feeling that Ying Chanxi was a bit irritable today after her afternoon nap.

He stood outside the three-point line, looked left and right, and in the end, chose to pass the ball to Qiao Xinyan.

Qiao Xinyan caught the basketball in a panic. She tried to dribble like Li Luo and the others, but she ended up just patting it like a toy ball. After a few pats, the ball rolled over into Yan Zhusheng's hands.

"You can just hug the ball and run. It's fine even if you play it like rugby, as long as you can get the ball in the hoop," Li Luo said with a smile.

He wasn't expecting the girls to learn how to dribble or anything anyway. The point was to play as they wished and for everyone to have a good time.

"Why aren't you going up to defend?" Li Luo glanced at Zhao Rongjun beside him. "My teammate is about to shoot."

Zhao Rongjun shook his head repeatedly. Watching the four girls crowded together under the basket, he absolutely did not dare to join the commotion.

Xu Youyu and the others, however, were playing with gusto, fighting over the ball and taking shots. Although it took them ages to score a single basket, it was quite fun.

Li Luo wasn't as polite as Zhao Rongjun. He specifically targeted Ying Chanxi, serving her a feast of blocked shots.

Ying Chanxi was tiny in front of him. Every ball she shot, Li Luo just had to reach out and scoop it into his hands.

Then he would pass the ball to Xu Youyu or Yan Zhusheng, who would smoothly put it through the hoop.

Ying Chanxi watched with her own eyes as he passed the ball to other girls, huffing indignantly and pouting without a word.

As a result, because she was too eager to score, she wasn't paying attention while fighting for a rebound and was hit on the head by the falling basketball.

"Ah!" Ying Chanxi was a bit dazed from the impact. She clutched her head and squatted on the ground. "Mmm..."

"Xixi, are you okay?" Xu Youyu quickly ran over and crouched beside Ying Chanxi to check on her.

"I'm fine." Ying Chanxi shook her head, rubbed her head, and then walked toward the long bench. "I'm just going to rest for a bit."

"You guys play first." Li Luo tossed the ball to Zhao Rongjun. "Teach them how to 'climb the turtle'."

"Oh, okay." Zhao Rongjun caught the ball and agreed.

Li Luo, on the other hand, walked to the long bench and squatted down in front of Ying Chanxi. He reached out to brush away the long hair that had fallen when she lowered her head and asked softly, "Where did it hit you?"

"I'm fine." Ying Chanxi turned her head away, not letting him see. "You don't need to worry about me. Go play with them."

"I saw you and Qiao Xinyan napping earlier, so I didn't call you." Li Luo reached out, pinched Ying Chanxi's soft, pink cheek, and turned her head to face him. He felt around on her head with his other hand. "Let me see, did it hit here?"

"Mmm..." Pinched by him, Ying Chanxi couldn't speak properly. She puffed up her cheeks to push his hand away, then lowered her head again and pointed to the front-left side of her head. "It hit here."

"Does it still hurt?" Li Luo gently rubbed it for her.

"...A little."

Li Luo let go, but Ying Chanxi immediately reached up and pressed his hand back onto the top of her head.

"I told you it still hurts a little. Why'd you let go?"

"...This hand is sore. Can't you let me switch hands, sis?"

"...Oh."

After a little while, both of Li Luo's hands were sore. Only then did he let go and sit down next to Ying Chanxi. "Is it better now?"

"A little better," Ying Chanxi said in a small voice.

In reality, it only hurt for a little while right after she was hit. By the time she sat down on the bench, she basically couldn't feel anything anymore.

After resting on the bench for a bit, the two of them returned to the court.

The six of them played all afternoon. Exhausted, they returned to Bihai Lanting. Li Luo had the four girls rest in the living room, then he dragged the able-bodied man into the kitchen, making Zhao Rongjun his assistant as they started cooking.

In the living room, Ying Chanxi looked at Yan Zhusheng, then turned to Xu Youyu. "Senior, will we be split into different classes in our second year?"

"Yeah," Xu Youyu nodded. "But at Fuzhong No. 1, the class assignments are announced after the National Day holiday. They're based on a combined score from last semester's final exams and this semester's entrance exam."

"What did you choose, Senior? The science stream or the liberal arts stream?"

"Liberal arts," Xu Youyu said with a grin. "Liberal arts is easier to study. It's all memorization, so you don't have to use your brain much."

That way, she would have more time to write her novels.

"Then how are the classes divided?" Ying Chanxi asked the question she was most concerned about.

"That." Xu Youyu recalled for a moment. "I think it's just based on grades?"

"For example, if there are over four hundred science students and over two hundred liberal arts students, then maybe Classes 1 to 10 will be science, and Classes 11 to 16 will be liberal arts."

"Then they're ranked by scores. Class 1 would be the best for science. For liberal arts, it's the other way around, with Class 16 being the best."

"I see." Ying Chanxi nodded in understanding, a sense of anticipation growing in her heart.

"Xixi, are you planning to choose liberal arts or science for your second year?" Xu Youyu asked curiously.

"I'm fine with either," Ying Chanxi shook her head. "They feel about the same. I might lean a little toward science, but liberal arts is fine too."

"What about you, Zhusheng?" Xu Youyu turned her head and asked.

"Me?" Yan Zhusheng blinked. "Can I only choose between science and liberal arts? My history and politics aren't great, and my physics is bad too. Can't I just choose chemistry, biology, and geography?"

Xu Youyu: "...That's not an option."

"Then I guess I can only choose the science stream," Yan Zhusheng thought for a moment and replied.

"And you, Xinyan?"

"Me? I'll probably choose liberal arts."

"What about Li Luo and Zhao Rongjun?" Xu Youyu shouted toward the kitchen.

"What?"

"Class assignments for the second year. Are you guys choosing liberal arts or science?"

"We'll see when the time comes," Li Luo said unhurriedly.

In his memory, their grade level wouldn't have a distinction between liberal arts and science.

The college entrance exam reform came down from out of nowhere, and they were the very first batch of experimental guinea pigs.

The moment Qianjiang Province's "3+3" and "7-choose-3" policies were released, it completely disrupted the previous arrangements of all the major high schools.

The competition for the college entrance exam instantly descended into a free-for-all.

(End of Chapter)
